newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Rating Corp assigns A rating to Sime Bank.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Rating Corp assigns A rating to Sime Bank.

text.p: The Malaysian Rating Corp Bhd (MARC) said on Wednesday it has assigned a long-term rating of A to Sime Bank Bhd, a unit of Sime Darby Bhd.
MARC said in a statement that Sime Bank has also been assigned its highest short-term rating of MARC-1.
Thomson BankWatch, Inc, the New York-based international rating agency which has a technical agreement with MARC, said it had rated Sime Bank IC-B/C as an intra-country issuer.

It has also assigned Sime Bank a short-term rating of LC-1, its highest.
Among MARC's long-term ratings, AAA is the highest.

The rating A reflected the "bank's improved asset quality and capital adequacy, satisfactory credit and treasury controls, the financial strength of its new shareholder and a capable and experienced management team," MARC said.
MARC said the bank has improved vastly since industrial conglemerate Sime Darby took it over last year.
"The bank, previously saddled with large amounts of non-performing loans, has since undertaken a major clean-up of its portfolio as borne out by the healthier non-performing loan ratio," MARC said.
It said Sime Bank's non-performing loan ratio dropped to 3.5 percent of total as at December 31, 1996, against 9.3 percent previously.
Sime Bank is the country's fifth biggest bank.
